questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: The rich culture and history of the city (Paris)

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: The french system was a little complicated to navigate in, but i found out and people there were friendly and wanted to help me.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: Assistance concerning how to subscribe to courses.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing through my host institution

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: I applied to live in Cité Universitaire, it was a part of my application to Sorbonne University so it was quite easy.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: Cité Universitaire is an amazing place... so many young people from all over the world and many social events.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: I had to show up fysically and fill a paper with the classes i wanted to follow. After that a woman from Sorbonne looked at the paper to see if it was possible and then approved.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: Help via email and help via going to the office.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I got the classes that i wanted without problems.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Be prepared, there is a day (friday before the semester starts) where you can sign up for classes but its a good idea to have chosen beforehand classes beforehand in order to make the process faster. Also there is a meeting earlier in that week where you get informations about subscribing for classes and other practical informations. Its a good idea attending that meeting.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA courses at your host university? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: It was a little too difficult for me in the beginning but later it got better. You should be realistic about your own level of french and academic level in general since it seems that the level is very high at Sorbonne.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: At Sorbonne it was more "old school" with the teacher speaking and sometimes uses the blackboard. At University of Copenhagen its more normal to use powerpoints and to upload files on the intranet, which for me is a very good thing. At Sorbonne it was more difficult to understand everything the teacher told us because there were not so many documents and files on the intranet (Moodle)

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
Histoire de la langue et sentiment de la langue
Rhétorique et stylistique
Poétique et rhétorique aux siècles classiques
Ecriture des savoirs et culture médiévale
Le francais de la renaissance

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Histoire de la langue et sentiment de la langue because it gave me an idea about the developpement of the french language during time. Le francais de la renaissance was good because it gave me an understanding of the renaissance in french, we read some of the famous author and got an idea about how humans at that time understood nature, other unknown cultures and the human nature.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: Not really any:)

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: The food, beer and wine are less expensive than expected. Same with the transport, i recommend to rent a bike from Swapfiets, its about 14 euros pr month and then you have it all the time. I rented it for 5 months and then delivred it back. Museums are also quite cheap, If you are younger than 26 the many things are free,for example museums.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: There is a group called Parismus Sorbonne, which is an organisation for Erasmus Students. They have a whatsapp and an Instagram account and have some different activities.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
Parties, day-trips or weekends trips to other cities. (watch the website called
Erasmusplace.com
for these trips).

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Normandy and Brittany, for example Honfleur Deauville, Saint Malo and Mont Saint Michel. Giverny is also nice and the same with Reims. They also have trips to South of France, for example Bordeaux which is a beautiful city.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: A little difficult because i didnt lived among local people (only two of the people from my floor are parisians).

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Talk to people from your class at Sorbonne. You can also get a language buddy via the app called Tandem (language exchange)

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: Parisians are a little reserved and not so open to foreigners.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The food, the appreciation of art and beauty, the archtecture and the café culture.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
Live in Cité Universitaire
Go explore Paris, there are some many things to discover
Say yes to things and be aware of all the differents whatsapp groups that organise events and parties.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Take some classes at Sorbonne that you are interested in, otherwise its gonna be tough. Start early on the exam-assignments of the classes.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Meeting new people and expanding my horizon. Getting to know a lot of amazing spots and places in Paris.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: To follow the classes in the beginning since it was some difficult subjects for me and it seems that the level of Sorbonne is quite high.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
